name: Vienna–Eastern Austria
rationale: Capital-region singleton; Vienna's national weight and distinct metropolitan/Pannonian character justify standalone representation, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

name: Austria outside Vienna (Styria–Carinthia–Tyrol–Salzburg–Upper Austria–Vorarlberg)
rationale: Non-capital Austria combined into one representation grouping; each Land keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity (Vorarlberg's special_status dual Swiss/Tyrolean orientation among them).

name: German-speaking Switzerland (Zürich–Basel–Bern–Ostschweiz)
rationale: All German-speaking Swiss cantons combined into one representation-weight bloc (Bern's federal-capital role stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased here); distinct from the French- and Italian-speaking language regions.

name: Romandie (French-speaking Switzerland)
rationale: Distinct national language community (French); not merged across the Röstigraben into German-speaking groupings.

name: Ticino (Italian-speaking Switzerland)
rationale: Distinct national language community (Italian); geographically separated by the Alps from the rest of Switzerland.

name: Alpine & Western European Microstates
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: five fully sovereign European microstates (populations ~800-90,000), each far too small individually for 40-70 representation weight. Clustered across borders per the explicit microstate convention; each remains its own cultural unit and sovereign state.

name: Alemannic Southwest (Baden-Württemberg)
rationale: Mirrors the real Land Baden-Württemberg (one Landtag, Stuttgart, since 1952). Baden/Württemberg split at the cultural-unit layer per Alemannic/Swabian dialect and pre-1952 statehood, reunited here for representation.

name: Bavaria (Franconia–Swabia–Altbayern)
rationale: Mirrors the real Land Bayern (one Bayerischer Landtag, Munich). Franconia/Bavarian Swabia/Munich-Altbayern split at the cultural-unit layer per distinct dialect/historic identity, reunited here for representation.

name: Western Germany (Hesse–Rhineland-Palatinate–Saarland–NRW)
rationale: Western German Länder along the Rhine-Main/Rhine-Ruhr-Saar corridor, geographically contiguous; each Land/historic region (Hesse, Rhineland, Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland) keeps its own cultural-unit identity, combined here for representation weight since five separate western blocs would push the count past the 40-70 target.

name: Hanseatic North Germany (Hamburg–Bremen–Schleswig-Holstein–Lower Saxony)
rationale: Contiguous North Sea/Low-German (Plattdüütsch) coastal Länder sharing Hanseatic trading heritage; grouped for representation weight while each city-state/Land keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

name: Neue Bundesländer / Eastern Germany (Saxony–Thuringia–Saxony-Anhalt–Berlin–Brandenburg–Mecklenburg-Vorpommern)
rationale: The standard German term 'Neue Bundesländer' for the former-East-Germany Länder plus Berlin, sharing post-1990 reunification/GDR administrative history; Berlin's capital-city weight stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

name: Flanders
rationale: Distinct Dutch-speaking community/Region with its own Parliament; large enough to stand alone.

name: Francophone Benelux (Wallonia–Brussels–Luxembourg)
rationale: Wallonia and Brussels share French-language civic space with neighbouring Luxembourg; Luxembourg is a small sovereign state clustering cross-border per convention, while each unit keeps its own identity/parliament.

name: Randstad (Amsterdam–Rotterdam)
rationale: The two Randstad conurbation units, contiguous and functionally integrated, kept distinct as cultural units (Amsterdam/Utrecht vs Rotterdam/Zeeland) but combined here for representation weight.

name: Nederland buiten de Randstad (Noord–Oost–Zuid)
rationale: Contiguous Dutch provinces outside the Randstad conurbation; Zuid-Nederland's distinct Catholic-south Brabantian/Limburgish identity preserved as its own cultural unit, combined here for representation weight.

name: Île-de-France (Paris)
rationale: Capital-region singleton; population and national weight justify standalone representation.

name: Nord-Ouest (Hauts-de-France–Normandy–Brittany–Pays de la Loire)
rationale: Contiguous northern/western France sharing a Channel-and-Atlantic-coast orientation; Brittany's distinct Breton/Celtic identity preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

name: Sud-Ouest (Aquitaine–Midi-Pyrénées)
rationale: Contiguous southwestern France, Gascon/Occitan cultural sphere.

name: Sud-Est (Languedoc-Roussillon–PACA–Corsica–Rhône-Alpes–Auvergne–Burgundy-Franche-Comté)
rationale: Contiguous southeastern quadrant of France; Corsica's distinct identity and Auvergne/Burgundy-Franche-Comté's split from Rhône-Alpes at the cultural-unit layer (Clermont-Ferrand vs Lyon vs Dijon/Besançon) preserved as separate cultural units, reunited here for representation weight since a six-bloc French layer would overshoot the 40-70 target.

name: Grand Est (Alsace–Lorraine–Champagne)
rationale: Contiguous northeastern France; Alsace's distinct Alemannic-German-influenced identity preserved as its own cultural unit.

name: Noroeste (Galicia–Asturias–Cantabria)
rationale: Contiguous Atlantic Celtic-tinged northern Spain, each region too small alone for the target; Galicia's own language preserved as its own cultural unit.

name: Noreste (Basque Country–La Rioja–Aragon)
rationale: Ebro-valley/Pyrenean neighbours of the Basque Country; Basque Country's distinct language/identity and own parliament preserved as its own cultural unit, grouped only for representation weight.

name: Madrid
rationale: Capital-region singleton.

name: Centro y Sur (Castile-León–Castile-La Mancha–Extremadura–Andalusia–Murcia–Ceuta y Melilla)
rationale: Contiguous inland-Meseta and southern Spain (Castile-La Mancha borders Andalusia/Murcia directly); each region and the special_status North-African exclaves keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity, combined here for representation weight.

name: Catalan-Speaking Mediterranean Arc (Catalonia–Valencia–Balearics)
rationale: Catalan/Valencian linguistic continuum along the Mediterranean coast (former Crown of Aragon); Catalonia and Valencia each keep distinct cultural-unit identity and own institutions.

name: Canary Islands
rationale: Atlantic archipelago, geographically and culturally distinct from mainland Spain; large enough to stand alone.

name: Gibraltar
rationale: British Overseas Territory, special_status; sovereignty distinct from Spain, kept a standalone singleton rather than merged into Spanish groupings.

name: Mainland Portugal (Lisboa–Alentejo–Algarve–Porto–Centro)
rationale: All mainland-Portugal cultural units combined into one representation grouping; each region (including Algarve's distinct tourism-region identity) keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

name: Atlantic Autonomous Regions (Azores–Madeira)
rationale: Portugal's two Atlantic autonomous-region archipelagos, each with own regional parliament, clustered here as remote island territories for representation weight.

name: Nord-Ovest (Piedmont–Liguria–Lombardy)
rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Nord-Ovest'.

name: Nord-Est (Veneto–Friuli–Trentino–South Tyrol–Emilia-Romagna)
rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Nord-Est', which spans Triveneto plus Emilia-Romagna; South Tyrol's special linguistic-autonomy status preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

name: Centro (Tuscany–Umbria–Marche–Lazio)
rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Centro', which includes Lazio/Rome alongside Tuscany, Umbria and Marche; Rome's national capital weight is a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

name: Mezzogiorno Continentale (Campania–Puglia–Abruzzo–Basilicata–Calabria)
rationale: Mainland-southern Italy, corresponding to the pre-unification mainland provinces of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies (roughly ISTAT 'Sud'); each region keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity (Neapolitan, Apulian, Calabrian etc.).

name: Isole (Sicily–Sardinia)
rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Isole'; Sicily and Sardinia each keep their own distinct island cultural-unit identity (Sicilian vs Sardinian, the latter its own Romance language) and special-statute autonomy, combined here only for representation weight.

name: Poland (Mazovia–Łódź–Małopolska–Eastern Poland–Silesia–Lower Silesia–Wielkopolska–Pomerania)
rationale: All eight Polish cultural units combined into one representation grouping; central/southeastern Poland (around Warsaw/Kraków) and western/northern Poland (former Prussian-partition sphere plus Baltic coast) each keep their own distinct regional cultural-unit identity (Silesian, Kashubian-Pomeranian etc.).

name: Czechia (Bohemia–Moravia–Czech Silesia)
rationale: All three Czech cultural units combined into one representation grouping, satisfying the 'Czech units -> 1-2 groupings' mandate at the low end; Bohemia and Moravia-Silesia each keep their own historic identity as cultural units.

name: Slovakia (Bratislava–East)
rationale: Both Slovak cultural units combined into a single representation grouping; each keeps its own identity (western Bratislava core vs eastern Košice/Prešov, with its Rusyn/Hungarian minority character).

name: Hungary (Budapest–West–Balaton–East/Debrecen)
rationale: All four Hungarian cultural units combined into one representation grouping, satisfying the mandated 'four Hungarian units -> 1-2 groupings' at the low end; Budapest's capital-city weight stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

name: Slovenia–Croatia
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small contiguous, EU-member, formerly-Yugoslav Adriatic states, clustered for representation weight (analogous to the Baltic States/South Caucasus clusters); each remains fully sovereign, Slovenia as its own cultural unit and Croatia's continental/Adriatic-coast regions each keeping their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: Western Balkans (Bosnia–Serbia–Montenegro–North Macedonia–Albania–Kosovo)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY/POLICY-BASED CLUSTER matching the EU's own 'Western Balkans' policy grouping (the six EU-enlargement candidates/entities of the region). Every member (Bosnia's three parliament-mandated entities, Serbia's Belgrade-core and autonomous Vojvodina, and the four small sovereign/de-facto states) keeps full cultural-unit identity and, where mandated, its own parliament; this grouping is purely a representation-weight bloc for otherwise very small/fragmented states, not a claim of shared identity.

name: Romania (Transylvania–Banat–Székely Land–Wallachia–Moldavia)
rationale: All five Romanian cultural units combined into one representation grouping; the historic Transylvanian bloc (including the Hungarian-Székely autonomous cultural unit) and the Old-Kingdom Wallachia-Moldavia core each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: Bulgaria (Sofia–Plovdiv–North Danube–Varna)
rationale: All four Bulgarian cultural units combined into one representation grouping; western/southern Bulgaria and the northern Danubian/Black-Sea regions each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: Athens–Attica
rationale: Capital-region singleton; roughly a third of national population, kept separate as with other large-country capitals (Paris, Madrid, Vienna).

name: Greece outside Attica (Macedonia–Thrace–Peloponnese–Crete–Aegean)
rationale: Non-capital Greece combined into one representation grouping; Macedonia (Thessaloniki) and Thrace (Komotini/Alexandroupoli) each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity per the mandated split.

name: Mediterranean Microstates (Cyprus–Malta)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small sovereign Mediterranean island EU member states, clustered across (non-contiguous) borders for representation weight per the microstate convention; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit (Cyprus's de-facto Greek/Turkish-Cypriot split stays flagged separately at the unit layer).

name: Manner-Suomi (Helsinki–Turku–Tampere–Oulu–Lapland–Lakeland)
rationale: Mainland Finland combined into one representation grouping (southern coastal belt plus interior/northern Finland including Sámi Lapland); each region keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: Åland
rationale: Swedish-speaking autonomous archipelago with its own parliament; kept a standalone singleton given its distinct autonomy status.

name: Stockholm (Östra Sverige)
rationale: Capital-region singleton, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

name: Sweden outside Stockholm (Gothenburg–Malmö–Gotland–Norrland)
rationale: Non-capital Sweden combined into one representation grouping; southern Sweden (including formerly-Danish Scania) and Norrland each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: Denmark (Copenhagen-Zealand–Jutland-Funen)
rationale: Mainland Denmark's two cultural units combined into one representation grouping.

name: Oslo Region (Eastern-Southern Norway)
rationale: Capital-region singleton, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

name: Norway outside Oslo (Vestlandet–Trøndelag–Nord-Norge)
rationale: Non-capital Norway combined into one representation grouping; the western fjord coast, Trøndelag and the Sámi north each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

name: North Atlantic (Iceland–Faroe Islands–Greenland)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: Iceland (sovereign) plus the Faroe Islands and Greenland (self-governing Danish Realm territories), clustered as small/remote North Atlantic territories for representation weight; each keeps its own sovereignty/autonomy status flagged at the unit layer.

name: Baltic States (Estonia–Latvia–Lithuania)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: three small sovereign Baltic states, each too small individually for 40-70 representation weight, clustered per the explicit Baltic convention; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit.

name: London
rationale: Capital-region singleton.

name: Southern & Midlands England (Sussex–Wessex–Solent–Exeter/Plymouth–Cornwall–Birmingham–East Midlands–Cambridge)
rationale: England outside London and the North, combined into one representation grouping since England alone would otherwise take an outsized share of the 40-70 budget; Cornwall's distinct Cornish identity preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

name: Northern England (Manchester–Liverpool–Lancashire–Yorkshire–Newcastle)
rationale: Consolidated 'Northern Powerhouse' belt (Lancashire/Yorkshire/North East), each metro area keeping its own cultural-unit identity; combined for representation weight since England alone would otherwise take an outsized share of the 40-70 budget.

name: Wales–Scotland
rationale: The two devolved Great Britain nations outside England (own Senedd/Holyrood), combined into one representation grouping; Wales and Scotland (Central Belt and Highlands) each keep their own distinct national/cultural-unit identity, not merged with any England grouping.

name: Northern Ireland
rationale: Kept a standalone singleton per the mandated distinct-unit-in-every-view treatment; not merged with Great Britain groupings or with the Republic of Ireland grouping given its distinct UK sovereignty status.

name: Ireland (Dublin–Cork–Galway)
rationale: Republic of Ireland's three cultural units combined into one representation grouping.

name: Crown Dependencies (Guernsey–Jersey–Isle of Man)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: three British Crown Dependencies (not part of the UK proper), each far too small individually, clustered per the explicit convention; each remains its own cultural unit.

name: Western & Central Ukraine (Lviv-Galicia–Volhynia–Zakarpattia–Kyiv–Hetmanate–Podillia)
rationale: Contiguous western and central Ukraine (historically Austro-Hungarian/Polish-influenced west, capital-region center); each region keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

name: Southern & Eastern Ukraine (Odesa–Crimea–Kharkiv–Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia–Donetsk–Luhansk)
rationale: Black Sea coast, Crimea and the eastern/Donbas oblasts (conflict_flags apply at the unit layer, unaffected by this representation-weight grouping); each region keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

name: Moldova
rationale: Sovereign state, single cultural unit; no adjacent small-state cluster fits without stretching geographic/cultural logic, kept standalone.

name: South Caucasus (Georgia–Armenia)
rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small contiguous sovereign South Caucasus states, clustered for representation weight; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit.

name: East Thrace
rationale: Isolated European sliver of Turkey (Turkey otherwise out of scope); kept a standalone, flagged singleton.
